name: OSME Trevor Poyser Species Conservation Fund

funder.name: Ornithological Society of the Middle East, the Caucasus and Central Asia (OSME)

summary: A single £5,000 award for a primarily field-based research and monitoring project on a globally threatened bird species in the OSME region; the project leader must be a national of the project country.

steps: Application and supporting documentation by email

eligibility.rule: Project leader is a country national
Target species is on the globally threatened list, or its population is shown to be nationally important
Project concept is compatible with an endorsed international species action plan when one exists
Applicant can receive the grant award via a bank transfer
Project starts during the following calendar year
Project is not a desk or laboratory study or an education or awareness raising project

calls.label: Call with 1 December deadline
calls.recurring: Applications are due by 1 December, for projects starting the following calendar year.
calls.note: The page gives the 1 December deadline without a year.

status.quote: Applications are considered once a year, and must be submitted on the standard application form.

recurring.quote: applications must be submitted by the 1st December for projects that must start during the following calendar year.

access.quote: Applications are considered once a year, and must be submitted on the standard application form.

window.quote: The deadline is the 1st December and applicants will usually be notified by the 31st December.

amount.quote: One award of £5000 is made each year

geography.quote: aimed specifically at individual species research and conservation projects within the OSME region

effort.quote: All applications and supporting documentation must be submitted by email in English.
The applications will be considered by the OSME Conservation Fund Committee and OSME Council

eligibility.quote: The project leader must be a country national, although collaboration with organisations and experts from outside the project country are encouraged.
Eligible species are listed in the table below. Consideration will be given to other species where the applicant can clearly show that the population is of national importance.
If the target species has an international species action plan endorsed by AEWA, CMS or IUCN, then the project concept must be compatible with the objectives and activities of that plan.
The project must be primarily field-based.
The project applicant must be able to receive the grant award via a bank transfer (please contact OSME if you have any concerns about this).
projects that must start during the following calendar year
Desk and/or laboratory-based studies. Education or awareness raising projects (but please check eligibility of the OSME Conservation Fund and Youth Development Fund).
